title: AgentArk: Distilling Multi-Agent Intelligence into a Single LLM Agent
claim: Multi-agent interaction can be generated, filtered into quality traces, and distilled through several strategies into one efficient single model.
layout: 3 panels, left-to-right; stages connected by arrows and a filter icon
description: A three-panel figure with rounded boxes, read left to right. The left panel is split in two. At the top, 'Input Data' (a database icon) and 'Expert Models' (a professor icon) feed down into a Multi-Agent Debate group. The debate shows four agent icons exchanging messages, ending in a Final Answer with a judge icon. Below that is a tree of colored reasoning nodes from a question x, with green checks and red crosses, and the final answers y* boxed in yellow dashes. A funnel icon marks knowledge extraction and leads to the middle panel. The middle panel shows four distillation variants: Standard SFT, Reasoning-Enhanced SFT, Distillation with Data Augmentation, and Process-Aware Distillation. Each uses a graduate-student icon, flame icons, PRM and GRPO labels, and contrastive learning. The right panel shows an Internalized Reasoning student, task icons (Reasoning, Math, Medical, QA, Summarization) and a radar chart comparing methods. Blue text labels and pastel node colors dominate.
caption: Overview of AgentArk: (1) Data Generation Through Multi-Agent Debate to produce diverse reasoning trajectories; (2) Knowledge Extraction to filters for high-quality corrective traces; and (3) Distillation utilizing Standard SFT, Reasoning-enhanced SFT, Distillation with Data Augmentation, and Process-Aware Distillation (PRM + GRPO).
abstract: While large language model (LLM) multi-agent systems achieve superior reasoning performance through iterative debate, practical deployment is limited by their high computational cost and error propagation. This paper proposes AgentArk, a novel framework to distill multi-agent dynamics into the weights of a single model, effectively transforming explicit test-time interactions into implicit model capabilities. This equips a single agent with the intelligence of multi-agent systems while remaining computationally efficient. Specifically, we investigate three hierarchical distillation strategies across various models, tasks, scaling, and scenarios: reasoning-enhanced fine-tuning; trajectory-based augmentation; and process-aware distillation. By shifting the burden of computation from inference to training, the distilled models preserve the efficiency of one agent while exhibiting strong reasoning and self-correction performance of multiple agents. They further demonstrate enhanced robustness and generalization across diverse reasoning tasks. We hope this work can shed light on future research on efficient and robust multi-agent development. Our code is at https://github.com/AIFrontierLab/AgentArk.
